tasks.short: Discuss land-use project purposes with planning officials.

steps.what: Prepare the project-purpose brief using existing verified parcel and proposal fields
inputs: existing land-use proposal and parcel records

steps.what: Discuss land-use purposes, competing needs and unresolved questions with planning officials
Write and approve actual agreed purposes, disagreements and follow-up actions
File the approved land-use discussion note
Send the approved discussion note to the internal planning officials

tasks.design: Use native planning-record brief templates ({OTHER}) to insert exact existing proposal/parcel facts, retaining context selection and checking. Keep the officials discussion and substantive outcome writing human. File and internally send the complete approved note as separate gated actions; no machine infers agreement or changes a land-use designation.
tasks.previous_blocker: A proposal description does not settle the actual purpose or reconcile competing needs.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing proposal fields can populate a checked factual brief without repeated copying.
tasks.still_hard: Public purpose, conflicting interests and actual agreement require discussion.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when officials mean different things by the same proposed use.
tasks.altitude: Less brief copying and note transfer with unchanged planning discussion.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: planning-record templates can reuse explicit proposal and parcel fields without interpreting project purpose.

assumptions: Shares are provisional. Establish actual repeated brief copying and note transfer; existing native templates earn no new benefit.

Applicant/project owner produces existing proposal_id, parcel_id, stated_use, description, area and source_version. s1 planner verifies applicability, selects fields and adapts/checks the complete brief in retained 12 hours per provisional 100. Missing/unstructured purpose is read and written manually, not freely extracted.

Officials produce actual discussion outcomes in s2; s3 planner separately captures agreed_purpose, disagreement, action_owner and next_action at full time before a1/a2. No planned outcome is treated as agreement.

This boundary assumes officials inside the employing planning authority; outside recipients require the actual external disclosure review/send. a1/a2 bind final note versions and their own destinations; edits revoke approval. Native features precede code.
research_questions: Which proposal facts are copied repeatedly into the purpose discussion brief despite native templates?

incremental.description: Maintain proposal field and note destination mappings

tasks.short: Stay informed about economic and legal issues in planning codes and environmental rules.

steps.what: Find relevant updates using native filters in authoritative planning and economic source registers
outputs: candidate planning economic and legal updates

steps.what: Read actual updates and verify scope, status, effective dates and economic context
inputs: candidate planning economic and legal updates

steps.what: Judge relevance to current land-use work and questions requiring specialist advice
Write and approve the update note, source status and practical limitations
File the approved planning issues note
Send the approved issues note to the internal planning team

tasks.design: Configure native topic/jurisdiction/date filters in existing authoritative legal and economic source registers ({OTHER}). Keep source reading, current-status checks, interpretation and update writing full time. The complete checked note is separately approved for filing and internal send; no legal effect or economic forecast is inferred by a model.
tasks.previous_blocker: An update title does not establish whether a rule is adopted, applicable or economically material.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing source metadata supports native filtering of candidate updates.
tasks.still_hard: Legal meaning and economic relevance require source reading and judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a proposal from an operative rule before changing planning advice.
tasks.altitude: Less update navigation with unchanged professional interpretation.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: authoritative source registers commonly support date/topic filters that retrieve candidate updates without interpreting their legal effect.

assumptions: Shares are provisional. Verify actual source-navigation and note-transfer work; existing subscriptions earn no new saving. No jurisdiction-specific legal claim is made here.

Official publishers/statistical sources produce title, publication_date, jurisdiction, topic and original document reference through their existing registers. Planner maintains filter terms and checks coverage in retained s1 time. No free custom tagging is assumed; unsupported sources use manual search.

s2 retains full reading and checks adopted/proposed status, effective_date and scope from original sources. s3 retains relevance and specialist-referral judgement. s4 separately writes/checks actual implications and caveats before a1/a2 bind final versions and destinations.
Changed sources require renewed review. Native subscriptions and document functions precede code; no rule update is silently applied to a project.
research_questions: Which authoritative sources still require repeated manual navigation after native topic filters are used?

incremental.description: Maintain source coverage and jurisdiction filters

tasks.short: Assess land-use proposal feasibility and identify necessary changes.

steps.what: Inspect proposal context, site conditions and actual planning requirements
Register and check proposal facts, source reports, revisions and assessment questions
inputs: actual transport, environmental and infrastructure reports

steps.what: Extract report constraints and check each suggested finding against its original passage

loop.purpose: Pre-read varied planning reports into a source-linked constraint evidence table
loop.input: Planner-selected actual reports, revisions and explicit assessment questions
loop.output: Candidate constraints, qualifications and conflicting passages with exact source locations
loop.check: Planner reads each cited passage and relevant surrounding sections, checks conditional wording, omissions and contradictory evidence against the full source package; no suggestion becomes a feasibility conclusion
loop.stop: Missing source, unsupported claim, material omission or two failed corrections returns the affected report to full manual reading
loop.why_not_simpler: Native indexes/checklists locate reports but cannot extract varying free-text qualifications; explicit facts and record registration already use deterministic handling

steps.what: Judge feasibility across site, infrastructure, environmental and planning constraints
Develop necessary proposal changes and write the reasoned feasibility assessment
outputs: complete candidate feasibility assessment and proposed changes

steps.what: Approve the complete feasibility assessment, changes and evidence limitations
inputs: complete candidate feasibility assessment and proposed changes

steps.what: File the approved final land-use feasibility assessment

tasks.design: Use native planning-record registration ({OTHER}) and document indexes first. Where varied source reports still require repeated extraction, a bounded model drafts a passage-linked constraints table in {DATA_PLATFORM}; the planner checks meaning, qualifications, omissions and conflicts. Site evaluation, feasibility judgement and required changes stay human; file only the approved completed assessment.
tasks.previous_blocker: A report summary may omit the qualification that changes feasibility.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded extraction can organise selected report passages for explicit planner verification.
tasks.still_hard: Cross-domain tradeoffs, site context and workable changes require planning judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Identify a feasible redesign rather than treat one report finding as an automatic refusal.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated constraint extraction with unchanged feasibility authority.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: bounded document extraction can propose source-linked constraints for full professional checking; it cannot establish planning feasibility.

assumptions: Shares are provisional. Measure actual repeated report extraction after native indexing; no existing report workflow/runtime earns a new saving. A pilot must test whether complete substantive review fits retained s3 time.

Applicant supplies proposal; named report authors supply actual versioned reports. s1/s2 planner verifies/captures proposal_id, parcel, proposed_use, quantities, report_id, author, revision, source pages and assessment questions at full time. No free tagging or assumed structured constraints. Unreadable or missing sources stay manual.

s3 retains 14 hours per provisional 100 for full semantic source checks and correction, including omitted/contradictory material; if needed review exceeds this, lower the saving or use full manual reading. Model output has no decision authority and unsupported passages are discarded.

s4/s5 retain feasibility and modification design/write time. s6 approves the actual complete assessment before a1 binds its version and project file. Edits revoke approval. No external decision, permit grant or notification is silently executed.
research_questions: After native indexing, can the table reduce repeated extraction while retaining complete source and omission checks?

already_counted.description: Semantic source checking and correction of candidate constraints

incremental.description: Sample extraction omissions and maintain report/version mappings

tasks.short: Determine how regulatory limitations affect land-use projects.

steps.what: Read applicable regulatory sources and verify jurisdiction, status, scope and effective dates
Map checked project facts to explicit numeric limits and source-qualified qualitative restrictions
Compare explicit project quantities with the checked numeric regulatory limits
outputs: numeric regulatory comparison results with source references

steps.what: Interpret regulatory effects, exceptions and interactions for the actual project
inputs: numeric regulatory comparison results with source references

steps.what: Write the effects assessment, necessary qualifications and unresolved specialist questions
Approve the complete regulatory effects assessment and source versions
Commit the approved regulatory effects assessment to the project record

tasks.design: Configure explicit numeric checks in the existing planning assessment system ({OTHER}). The planner reads the actual rules, captures their applicability and project facts, and interprets all legal effects and exceptions. The numeric comparison cannot grant compliance; write and approve the complete human effects assessment before its separate commit.
tasks.previous_blocker: An exceeded limit alone does not establish its applicability or the effect of an exception.
tasks.enabler_now: Native assessment checklists can compare explicit verified quantities with explicit limits.
tasks.still_hard: Meaning, interactions and project-specific consequences require professional interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: Identify when a seemingly simple numeric result depends on an unresolved definition or exception.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated numeric checking with unchanged regulatory interpretation.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: planning checklists can compare explicitly mapped project quantities with numeric limits while leaving applicability and legal effects to a planner.

assumptions: Shares are provisional. Check actual manual numeric comparisons after native system features; no existing automatic check earns a new saving. This describes a workflow and asserts no particular jurisdictions legal rule.

Official publisher supplies actual rules; project designer supplies verified quantities/drawings. s1 planner verifies sources; s2 captures project_id, quantity_name, value, unit, rule_reference, rule_version, numeric_limit, operator, applicability rationale and qualitative restrictions at full time. Missing or disputed definitions remain manual rather than inferred.

s3 executes only explicit numeric comparisons. Applicability, exceptions, qualitative limits and effect determination stay fully human in s4. If no formal numeric comparison applies, s3 has no new saving. Native checklist configuration precedes code.
s5 writes the actual reasoned assessment; s6 checks its complete final version before a1. Edits revoke approval. No permit decision, external notification or project change is performed.
research_questions: Which repeated quantity-to-limit comparisons can the native system perform without automating regulatory interpretation?

incremental.description: Verify numeric rule versions and project-unit mappings

approvals.approved_version: s6 complete regulatory effects assessment and project destination

role.altitude: Use explicit sources and controlled records to support human land-use and regulatory judgement.
reach: Help project colleagues distinguish source evidence, calculated checks and actual planning conclusions.
role.ambitious_version: A planner who grounds practical land-use advice in traceable sources while preserving discussion, site knowledge and professional interpretation.
